The current low-level goals (LLGs) cover the essential aspects of the parent high-level goal (HLG). They include selecting a pickup time slot, receiving reminders for missed pickups, handling order forfeiture due to non-collection by Friday, and updating the fair-play score based on pickup compliance. Each LLG is well-defined, supported by documented interactions or effects, and does not show redundancy or out-of-scope elements.

The 'Select pickup time slot' (llg_001) is a documentary automatic effect as it does not require manual triggering by the customer. The system provides available slots based on store availability, aligning with the parent's description of providing customers with time slots for product collection.

The 'Receive pickup reminder notification' (llg_002) and 'Receive missed pickup notification' (llg_003) are also documentary automatic effects. They support the parent's requirement to notify customers about their pickup times and consequences of missing them, respectively.

The 'Automatically mark order as forfeited if not collected by Friday' (llg_004) and 'Update fair-play score upon forfeit or missed pickup' (llg_005) are essential for enforcing system reliability and maintaining precedence criteria based on customer reliability. These LLGs align with the parent's description of handling forfeited orders and updating scores accordingly.

No unsupported, misleading, or missing capabilities were identified in the current LLGs. They collectively and completely realize the parent HLG through documented functional interactions or effects, adhering to the actor criterion of document-supported automatic notifications and system operations that do not require manual triggering by the customer actor.
